h1: The 6 Best Bath Transfer Boards and Benches of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Bath Transfer Boards: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 6 bath transfer boards and benches compared on stated capacity, tub width fit, backrest, seat height range and material.
summary: The DMI Tub Transfer Bench is the best choice for most users who need full support, with a backrest, a safety belt and the highest stated capacity at 400 lb. The Drive Medical bench lets you set seat height in half-inch steps, the FinityPro rotates 360 degrees for a seated turn, and the PEPE board suits lighter users with good trunk control.
intro: A transfer board and a transfer bench look similar and do different jobs. A board bridges a gap, from a wheelchair to a shower seat, and you slide across it. A bench straddles the tub wall, with two legs outside and two inside, so you sit outside the tub, then swing your legs over. Buying a board when you need a bench is the usual mistake, and in a wet bathroom it matters.

We ranked six products from the listings: type, stated capacity, tub width fit, backrest, seat height range, material and whether a handle or belt is included. Capacity figures are maker ratings and the tub width must match. These are safety-related aids, so a physical or occupational therapist should check the fit and technique for your bathroom.

products.name: DMI Tub Transfer Bench with Backrest
products.verdict: A 400 lb bench on a rust-resistant aluminum frame with a backrest, safety belt and a 19 to 23.5 inch seat.
products.description:
The DMI Tub Transfer Bench has a rust resistant aluminum frame, a stated 400 lb capacity, a seat height of 19 to 23.5 inches, a backrest, a safety belt and an install that works for a right or left tub.

It ranks first because it has the highest stated capacity here and the fullest support, with a backrest and belt for users who tire easily. It edges the Drive Medical on capacity, 400 lb against 350 lb, though the Drive offers finer height steps. It is a bench, so it needs room beside the tub.

Buy it if you need full support and a high rating. Skip it if your bathroom is too tight for a bench.
products.idealFor: Users who need full support and a high rating.
products.skipIf: Your bathroom is too narrow for a bench.

products.name: Drive Medical Tub Transfer Bench, 350 lb
products.verdict: A 350 lb bench with a backrest, drainage openings and seat height set in half-inch steps.
products.description:
The Drive Medical bench has an aluminum frame, a stated 350 lb capacity, a backrest, drainage openings and seat height adjustment in 0.5 inch steps.

It ranks second because half-inch steps let you match the seat to your tub wall precisely, which affects how smoothly you swing a leg over. It trails the DMI on capacity and on the safety belt, which the listing does not mention. Drainage openings keep water from pooling.

Buy it if you want a backrest and precise seat height. Skip it if you need more than 350 lb.
products.idealFor: Users who need a backrest and exact seat height.

products.name: FinityPro Rotating Tub Transfer Bench with Handle
products.verdict: A 360 degree rotating seat rated for 300 lb, fitting tubs from 18 to 26.5 inches wide.
products.description:
The FinityPro has a 360 degree rotating seat, a stated 300 lb capacity, fits tubs 18 to 26.5 inches wide, has a safety handle and weighs 5.6 lb.

It ranks third because a rotating seat means you turn without twisting your hips, which is the difficult part of a tub transfer. It costs less, at $25-50, but it is a lighter-duty board, and it has no backrest listed.

Buy it if a seated turn helps and your tub width fits. Skip it if you need a backrest.
products.idealFor: Users who benefit from a seated turn.

products.name: PEPE Mobility Bath Board with Handle, Model 2
products.verdict: A 5.5 lb polypropylene bath board with a handle, four adjustable legs and a 242 lb limit.
products.description:
The PEPE Mobility board is polypropylene, with a 242 lb maximum user weight, a fit for tubs 15.5 to 24.5 inches wide, four adjustable legs, a handle and a weight of 5.5 lb.

It ranks fourth because it is light and easy to move, but 242 lb is the lowest limit here and it has no backrest. It suits users who still have good trunk control.

Buy it if you are lighter and have trunk control. Skip it if you need a backrest or higher capacity.
products.idealFor: Lighter users with good trunk control.

products.name: suboton Transfer Board with Slide Sheet 31.5 in
products.verdict: A 31.5 inch board with a 28 inch slide sheet, anti-slip back and three handles.
products.description:
The suboton set pairs a 31.5 by 8 inch board with a 28 by 28 inch slide sheet, an anti-slip back, three handles and curved edges.

It ranks fifth because it reaches a shower chair or tub seat and moves beyond the bathroom, but it is a bridge, not a bench, and it does not carry a stated capacity in the listing. The slide sheet reduces friction.

Buy it if you need a board for several rooms. Skip it if you need a bench inside the tub.
products.idealFor: Users who need a board for a shower chair and elsewhere.

products.name: Buckingham Healthcare Glideboard Transfer Board
products.verdict: A premium polymer board at 27.75 x 13.5 inches with a detachable sliding seat, rated 300 lb.
products.description:
The Buckingham Glideboard is premium polymer at 27.75 by 13.5 by 0.75 inches, rated for 300 lb, with a detachable sliding seat that cleans with soap and water.

It ranks last for bath use because it is a wheelchair transfer board that works in more places than the bathroom, and costs $100-200. It is wide and easy to clean.

Buy it if you move between a wheelchair and many seats. Skip it if you want a tub bench.
products.idealFor: Wheelchair users who want an easy-clean gliding seat.
products.skipIf: You want a bench for tubs.

whatMatters.detail: A board bridges a gap and a bench straddles the tub wall. A bench keeps you seated through the whole transfer, while a board needs sliding. Check the type on the listing, and ask a therapist which matches your ability. Wet porcelain is slippery, so the fit and the seat angle matter more than any extra feature, and a therapist can watch you make a transfer.

Capacity is the maker's weight rating, from 242 to 400 lb here. Pick a rating above your weight, since wet surfaces add stress. Check the rating on the listing. Leave a margin, because the figure assumes a static load on a dry seat and a transfer adds movement and shock.

A bench or board must span the tub wall, and the listing gives a width range such as 15.5 to 24.5 inches. Measure your tub across the top and compare it with the range. Measure at the widest and narrowest points of the rim, since many tubs have a curved or sloped edge.

A backrest and safety belt help users who tire or lean. Look for them on the listing. A rotating seat, like the FinityPro's, helps a seated turn. Without a backrest, trunk control becomes the safety factor, which is why the lighter boards suit steadier users.

Aluminum resists rust and polypropylene wipes clean. Drainage openings stop water pooling. Check the material and holes on the listing, and clean the legs to keep rubber feet gripping. Rubber feet wear, so replace them if they harden or slip.

faq.q: Can a transfer bench fit any tub?
faq.a: Only within its listed range. A narrow tub suits the PEPE, a wider one suits the FinityPro, and the DMI adjusts in between. Measure the top of your tub before ordering. A therapist can double check any fit.

faq.q: What is the most common mistake?
faq.a: Buying a board when you need a bench. The suboton and Buckingham bridge a gap, while the DMI and Drive Medical straddle the tub wall. Never use a bench on a tub it does not fit.

faq.q: Is the DMI worth it over the Drive Medical?
faq.a: For a higher capacity and a belt, yes. The DMI is rated 400 lb with a safety belt, while the Drive Medical is rated 350 lb with half-inch steps. The added support is worth the premium if you tire quickly.

faq.q: How do I set one up?
faq.a: Place the legs on a dry floor, with two inside the tub and two outside, then set the height. A therapist can check the install. Check that every foot is flat and dry before you sit.

faq.q: How do I look after it?
faq.a: Rinse after use and dry the legs and rubber feet so they grip. Check for loose bolts. Wipe it dry to prevent soap film.

faq.q: Does a transfer bench need a shower curtain?
faq.a: A curtain still hangs over the bench side. Use a curtain with a liner and keep water in the tub. Keep the curtain tucked inside the tub.

finalTake: The DMI Tub Transfer Bench with Backrest is the best buy for users who need full support, with 400 lb, a backrest and a safety belt. The Drive Medical offers half-inch height steps, the FinityPro turns on a rotating seat, and the suboton and Buckingham are bridge boards. Check tub width and ask a therapist to confirm the fit.
